ai.summary: Reuters reports that Jensen Huang misled senior Nvidia leaders about his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman, citing people familiar with the matter and internal correspondence. The story comes amid a board investigation and Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO, with potential implications for leadership at the AI chipmaker.
ai.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO misled top lawyer on affair with Chinese businesswoman, sources say

ai.summary: A coalition of nonprofits sued OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, and SpaceX’s AI division, seeking to block further development of advanced AI models. The complaint argues that California unfair-business-practices law supports an injunction, though the case’s outcome and potential reach are uncertain.
ai.title: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic hit with lawsuit to halt AI development

ai.summary: Chinese AI companies are reportedly seeking access to Nvidia-powered computing at overseas data centers, amid concern that US rules could tighten restrictions on remote access to advanced chips. The report, based on people familiar with the matter, highlights a potential enforcement challenge for export controls.
ai.title: Chinese AI firms rush to secure Nvidia chip capacity as spy scandal stirs fear of US curbs

ai.summary: Anthropic reported that Claude Fable 5.1’s performance on multi-turn safety evaluations differed substantially between its API and claude.ai configurations, by as much as 34 percentage points. The findings underscore that model behavior can vary with deployment setup and system prompts.
ai.title: Anthropic reports configuration differences in Claude safety evaluations

ai.summary: Finnish logician Jan von Plato told The Guardian that Claude helped transcribe and analyze Kurt Gödel’s shorthand notebooks, surfacing hundreds of theorems from the material. The account describes AI as an aid to a long-running scholarly effort, not independent verification of the results.
ai.title: Gödel’s notebooks and the use of Claude in extracting theorems

quantum.summary: Atom Computing finalized an agreement for up to $100 million from the U.S. Department of Commerce to advance research and development of fault-tolerant, utility-scale neutral-atom quantum systems. The funding is intended to support engineering, testbed capacity and system performance.
quantum.title: Atom Computing Finalizes $100 Million U.S. Department of Commerce R&D Agreement for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Systems

quantum.summary: Researchers from AMD and IBM Research reported near-linear scaling for the Pêlagos quantum-error-correction decoder across as many as eight GPUs. The work, tested on AMD accelerators and deployed on Oak Ridge’s Lux system, aims to speed large-scale QEC simulation.
quantum.title: Pêlagos Achieves Near-linear GPU Scaling

quantum.summary: Researchers from RIKEN and Toshiba described an encoder for a [[30,6,5]] symplectic double code, designed to prepare encoded states with fewer resources. The report says the method uses 67 gates, compared with 108 for the standard approach, and targets more practical experiments with high-rate error-correcting codes.
quantum.title: A [[30,6,5]] Code May Allow Quantum Experiments To Scale Up Faster

quantum.summary: IBM reportedly unveiled the 520-qubit Nighthawk r3 superconducting processor, claiming improved two-qubit gate fidelity and circuits capable of 10,000 two-qubit operations. The available report describes benchmark and engineering claims but does not link to an IBM announcement.
quantum.title: IBM introduces the 520-qubit Nighthawk r3 processor, boosting two-qubit gate fidelity

quantum.summary: A preprint by researchers at Harvard, Anthropic and QuEra reports that Claude helped design quantum circuits with lower resource requirements in seven of eight studied building blocks. The results are resource estimates, not demonstrations on quantum hardware.
quantum.title: Claude designs quantum circuits with lower resource demands

quantum.summary: A report on work by researchers at LUMS and KAUST describes a batched parameter-shift method for training quantum neural networks that could reduce quantum-processor job submissions. In simulations involving models with 24 to 48 parameters, it required about one-fifth to one-half as many jobs as SPSA methods.
quantum.title: Quantum Neural Networks May Need Fewer Cloud Jobs With New Method
